section_1.title: Prerequisites: The Geometry of a Cone
section_1.content: Define a right circular cone and a cutting plane. Introduce the 'Double Cone' concept to set the stage for all conic types.
section_1.example: Imagine a flashlight beam expanding in a dark room; the light forms a cone, and the wall acts as our cutting plane.

section_2.title: Introducing the Dandelin Spheres
section_2.content: Explain the concept of spheres inscribed within the cone, tangent to both the cone (along a circle) and the cutting plane (at a single point). These points of tangency are the 'Foci'.
section_2.example: Visualize a marble (sphere) dropped into an ice cream cone until it gets stuck—the circle where it touches the cone is the contact ring.

section_3.title: Connecting the Geometry to the Conic
section_3.content: Show how the distance from any point on the conic section to the foci relates to the distance to the directrix. Explain that the tangency points of the Dandelin spheres provide the geometric proof for these relationships.
section_3.example: A rabbit (the point on the conic) moves such that its distance to a 'carrot' (the focus) and a 'fence' (the directrix) maintains a constant ratio.

section_4.title: The Visual Transformation
section_4.content: Use a progressive animation: Tilt the plane to transition from a circle (parallel to base) to an ellipse, then a parabola, and finally a hyperbola (parallel to the cone's edge). Show how the Dandelin sphere moves accordingly.
section_4.example: An animation of a laser cutter slicing through a 3D model of a cone, changing the angle of the cut to reveal the four conic sections in real-time.

section_5.title: Conclusion and Application
section_5.content: Summarize that Dandelin spheres bridge the gap between 3D solids and 2D curves, proving that conic sections aren't just arbitrary equations but fundamental geometric properties.
section_5.example: Satellite orbits (ellipses/hyperbolas) and the physics of how a telescope dish (parabola) focuses starlight to a single point—the focus!

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Visual Transformation", [
            "Tilt the plane to change the shape.",
            "The circle transforms into an ellipse.",
            "Steeper cuts create parabolas and hyperbolas.",
            "Spheres shift to match the new slice.",
            "Every cut maintains its fundamental property."
        ])

        # Define objects
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1.5, height=3).rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT)
        plane = Plane(normal=OUT).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.5).scale(1.5)
        
        # Position objects
        self.place_at_grid(cone, 'D3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(plane, 'D3', scale_factor=0.7)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(cone), FadeIn(plane))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        # Animate tilt
        self.play(Rotate(plane, angle=PI/6, about_point=self.grid['D3'], axis=UP))
